summary: Redis is at its configured memory ceiling. Eviction began before latency rose and the log shows write refusals in the same window, so memory pressure is the cause rather than a consequence.

hypotheses.statement: Redis reached maxmemory; eviction could not free space fast enough.
hypotheses.rationale: Used memory is above 90% of maxmemory and eviction precedes the latency rise.

hypotheses.statement: A single slow command blocked the event loop.
hypotheses.rationale: CPU stayed below saturation and no long fork pause was observed.

findings.statement: Used memory is above 90% of the configured maxmemory.
findings.detail: At this point Redis either evicts keys or refuses writes, depending on maxmemory-policy.

checks_passed: The instance was reachable throughout the window.
No long fork pause was observed.

gaps.impact: node-level memory pressure could not be ruled out

recommendations.statement: Confirm the eviction policy with CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy.
recommendations.rationale: The policy decides whether clients see errors or silent data loss.

recommendations.statement: Raise maxmemory only if the host has headroom.
recommendations.rationale: Without headroom the kernel OOM killer replaces a degraded Redis with a dead one.
